title: Capacity Gesture Strip — compact quick-controls for Dedicated GPU pools
creator: Lina Ortega
description:
Problem: Operators need a very small surface in the Redwood Console to perform common Dedicated pool actions (adjust autoscale bands, trigger short bursts, mute autoscale temporarily) without navigating into heavy dashboards. Existing pool UIs are information-dense and require multiple clicks for common run-of-day tasks.

Goal: Design a compact, low-friction "Capacity Gesture Strip" — a 1-row control strip that sits at the top of pool detail views and in a fleet quick-actions panel. It should expose the most used controls with clear affordances, lightweight confirmations, and contextual states (e.g., plan pending, capacity locked, recent burst). The strip must work responsively down to narrow side panels and be accessible per Redwood console patterns.

Scope: Visual UI (icons, microcopy), interaction states, micro-confirm flows, accessibility labels, small prototype for usability testing, and handoff tokens for implementation. Not in scope: backend autoscale policy changes, new telemetry schemas (handled by ENG tickets), or RBAC plumbing beyond showing/hiding controls.
acceptance_criteria: A compact strip prototype (Figma) with 4 core controls: Autoscale toggle + quick slider, Burst action (30s & 5m presets), Capacity lock (prevent autoscale), and Cost/Impact preview chip.
Micro-interaction spec for each control including hover, active, disabled, and pending states documented in Confluence with CSS tokens.
Accessible patterns: keyboard focus order, ARIA labels for all controls, and contrast-compliant icons per WCAG AA.
Usability test session (5 ops+platform engineers) completed and feedback captured; top-3 changes iterated in prototype.
Implementation-ready handoff: exported components, measurements, copy, and a short dev checklist referencing ENG dependencies.
Design sign-off from PM (Arielle Chen) and Eng lead (Ravi Kapoor) recorded in ticket comments.
Prototype wired to a mocked telemetry panel showing estimated incremental cost and expected latency impact when toggling burst or changing slider.
Edge cases documented: network failure during burst trigger, race with concurrent autoscale policy rollout, and hidden controls for read-only roles.
decisions: Kept the control set to four primary actions to minimize cognitive load. Rejected inline freeform numeric tweaker in favor of a compact slider with +/- microbuttons to prevent accidental large commits. Burst presets limited to 30s and 5m based on telemetry of common operator usage; 'custom' burst moved to full pool detail view. Cost preview shown as a non-blocking chip that expands on hover — avoids modal interruptions. Accessibility: chose filled iconography for high contrast and added explicit aria-describedby on controls to expose cost/impact copy to screen readers.
